narrative:
The model estimates an 11% chance that you will fail your final year, which is low but enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. While this is generally positive, in this case it appears the model sees your clean record as less protective than it does for other students who passed, possibly because other parts of your profile suggest you may be at risk of slipping. Second, the quality of your family relationships is described as good, yet this still pulled the prediction slightly toward failing compared with students who passed. Third, your strong desire to pursue higher education is a clear positive signal that works against failure, but its protective effect was not strong enough to outweigh the other influences.

Taken together, these elements led the model to recommend extra support. To improve, you should focus on building consistent study habits beyond your current 2–5 hours per week, make the most of the extra educational support you already receive, and talk openly with your family about how they can help you stay on track. Strengthening these areas now can turn the modest risk into a clear success. (218 words)
